M. Baratt, `The Library of John Selden and its Later History', BLR 3 (1951), 128-42; John Sparrow, `The Earlier Owners of Books in John Selden's Library', BQR 6 (1931), 263-71; The Bodleian Library in the Seventeenth Century, Guide to an Exhibition (Oxford, 1951), 43-7; Philip 47-8; Rogers, Treasures, 121, 130-1; A. L. Rowse, Four Caroline Portraits (London, 1993), 125-55; Graham Parry, The Trophies of Time: English Antiquaries of the Seventeenth Century (Oxford, 1995), ch. 4; Toomer, Eastern Wisedome, ad indicem, esp. 64-71; Sandra Naiman, `John Selden (1584-1654)', in Pre-Nineteenth-century British Book-collectors and Bibliographers, ed. William Baker and Kenneth Womack, DLB 213 (Detroit, Washington DC, and London, 1999), 297-306; Reid Barbour, John Selden: Measures of the Holy Commonwealth in Seventeenth-century England (Toronto, 2003); the catalogue now kept as MS. Selden supra 111 was drawn up at Selden's house in London, probably shortly after his death; MS. Broxb. 84.10 and MS. Add. C. 40 were drawn up at the Bodleian Library in 1672, the former for Chief Justice Vaughan, the other for another of Selden's executors; some of Selden's books bear his motto `περί παντός την ελευθερίαν'.

provenance.note:
Sul contropiatto anteriore collocazione dell'attuale Biblioteca indicante la provenienza Cicogna.
Precedono il testo 9 carte manoscritte da E.A. Cicogna. Sulla sesta carta manoscritta Cicogna racconta il: 'modo con cui ottenni questo veramente raro officietto. Essendo venuto a Venezia nell'estate 1854 il chiarissimo Sig. commendatore Francesco Rossi figlio del fu Gherardo di Roma, colla principessa Carlotta di Borbone, duchessa di Sassonia, sua moglie, comperò fra varii preziosi libri anche questo Officietto dal librario Gaetano Canciani il quale fu così buono di cederglielo per sole lire sedici austriache. A questa notizia, mi lamentai, a dir vero col Canciani, .... '. 
Francesco Rossi di lì a poco si ammalerà e morirà nel settembre del 1854 a Venezia. Cicogna, per non perdere il libro d'ore,  si mise  in contatto la duchessa Carlotta di Borbone, che nel frattempo era partita da Venezia, e riuscirà poi a farsi regalare l'opera.
In fine altra annotazione manoscritta contenente una breve nota di Cicogna su Raffaele Zovenzenio.
Emmanuele Antonio Cicogna lasciò la sua biblioteca al Museo civico per disposizione testamentaria del 1865, perfezionata alla sua morte tre anni dopo.

In Philelphus’ book, marginal notes in a neat fifteenth-century humanist hand, light-brown-green ink, extracting key words. On the last leaf, after some notes in Latin and Greek, an inscription in Italian, dated 18 Mar. 1510: «In Christi nomine amen. Et sia noto et manifesto come la reuerentia fe patre Pietro de Bonetti se obliga a celebrare ogni sabbato una messa a la ecclesia de Sancta Maria de la Consolatione in Bressa Ad instantia de M.co. Io. Baptista di Bonetti suo fratello (?) questo come zanoso(?) adi 18 de Mazo 1510 [...] M.ro Zuanne di Bonetti suo padre [...]».
The note relates that father Pietro Bonetti, a priest, promises to celebrate a mass every Saturday in the church of S. Maria de la Consolazione, Brescia, on request of his brother, Giovanni Battista Bonetti, for some reason relating to their father, probably to commemorate his death.

provenance.decorationNote: Woodcuts painted over in gold and colours. On a1r, f2r, h3r, l7r, and m2r full borders are supplied in gold and colours, by a close follower of Matteo Felice (fl. 1467-1493), perhaps a member of his workshop. On a1r and f2r the border contains putti, a peacock, a hare, foliate decoration in blue, purple, and green, filigree and gold bezants, all enclosed within a frame of gold and another of blue. On h3r and l7r the border contains also a bird; on m2r there is a stag and one putto wears a breastplate.  Main initials contain the following miniatures: on e7v Virgin and child, on f2r David praying, on h3r a coffin covered by a drape, behind stand a priest and fours monks praying, with a tall pole with cross on top, on l7r Christ on the cross, surrounded by the instruments of the Passion, on m2r Descent of the Holy Spirit. The initials on e7v, f2r, h3r, l7r, m2r, are supplied in purple with green foliate edges and blue inside the letter, all with white penwork, within a gold ground, and with floral extension from the letter into the margin in blue, purple, green, and gold bezants. Other main initials are supplied in gold on a shaped blue ground with white penwork, the area enclosed by the letter is purple with white penwork, or the reverse; sometimes it can also consist of a chequered ground red and blue; occasionally a pen extension from the letter forms foliate decoration and gold bezants. In the calendar the letters «KL» are supplied in gold with violet penwork. On a1r coat of arms in the lower panel of the border; azure, a cock proper crested and jellopped, on a chief argent two flowers(?) gules.

provenance.msNote: Additions to the calendar in a sixteenth-century hand: 17 Sept. «Stigmata sancti Francisci»; in the upper margin of [A9r] «Sancti Caroli Cardinalis Borromei Archiep Mediolan. »; next to s Prosdocimi (7 Nov.) added «Patavini», all in the same hand. Bound at the end are nine parchment leaves of manuscript prayers and suffrages, with painted miniatures of St George killing the dragon; St Jacobus ap; St Augustine; St Sebastianus; Leonardus cf; Cristophoro; Antonio cf; the crucifixion, behind, a landscape, next, the prayer: «Domine deus meus si feci uel commisi... ». These additions begin with capitals in blue with red penwork decoration. -- More prayers in a later hand, in Latin and in Italian, washed. -- Arabic numerals were added to calendar in an early hand. In the litanies, «Nicolae de Tollentino» was added in the margin between Innocentes and Stephane; «sce Anelle» was added after Ianuari, «sce Iuliane» before Nicolae; a name now erased before Bernarde; «Sancta Anna» before M. Magdalena; «Sta Martha» between Agatha and Clara; all in a contemporary hand, brown ink.

Al contropiatto anteriore: "OP 2241" (i volumi raccolti dall'Oppizzoni recano il suo monogramma OP seguito dal numero progressivo corrispondente a quello del suo registro degli acquisti, cioè il "Catalogo dei libri acquistati ...").
Il "Catalogo de' libri acquistati dal fu monsignor Gaetano Oppizzoni" riporta l'acquisto di questo volume in data 17 gennaio 1829.
Il conte Antonio Greppi era per testamento erede universale di monsignor Gaetano Oppizzoni.

stampsNote: A c. a2r, timbro circolare in inchiostro nero recante lo stemma della famiglia Oppizzoni (troncato, nel 1° d'oro all'aquila di nero coronata del campo; nel 2° d'argento a tre palle di rosso, 2 e 1; lo scudo è accollato all'aquila bicipite imperiale) con legenda nella corona esterna: BIB. OPPIZZONI. CAP. METROPOL. MILANO.
provenance.note: Il conte Antonio Greppi decise la "cessione in uso perpetuo" dei libri di monsignor Gaetano Oppizzoni alla Biblioteca Capitolare del Duomo di Milano; tale cessione (documentata dall’atto notarile rogato dal notaio Giuseppe Alberti e attestata dal timbro apposto per l’occasione sul volume), non in piena proprietà, voleva garantire l'integrità della raccolta nel caso di future confische. La donazione costituì il nucleo di partenza per la ricostruzione della Biblioteca Capitolare, dispersa a seguito delle soppressioni degli enti religiosi disposte dalla Repubblica Cisalpina.

records.physicalDescriptionNote:
On vellum. Rubricated. Each line of text between red rules. Woodcuts heavily coloured. Part of the small woodcut at the head of Mayus-Iunius has been cut away. At the end are bound 27 additional leaves of vellum, bearing a 'Cursus de passione Christi' and a 'Cursus pro defunctis in manuscript'. On 1a is the signature of Johan Wilhelm Zur Madten, Altrath [of Solothurn?], 1657, in the top the armorial book-plate of Urs. Hos. Nic. Louis Glutz de Blozheim [of Solothurn], conseiller d'état, cy-dev. officier au service de Sardaigne, and on a fly-leaf the signature of Conrad Gluz von Blozheim, canonicus in Solothurn. At the foot of 1b is written: Ex dono D.ae B. n.tae B. a. 1781. Old black morocco (BMC).
The manuscript bound at the end mainly contents the two texts (Cursus de Passione Christi and a Cursus pro defunctis) written in 15th century bastard. Later, on the last leaf a list of saints has been added in a very different handwriting (antiqua in the shape used in the 18th century), listing many modern saints including several Jesuits.
Manuscript notes are mainly in German; there are also in French and Latin; e.g. on v8r three hands, four sentence, two in German, one in Latin (Deliberandum est diu, quod statuendum est semel) one in French (Fay bien Laysser dire). The portion of woodcut cut off on b4 is likely evidence of censorship, as the image represented the twins (the Gemini) naked.

Auf VD / HD durchbrochene Messingrahmen (Kreuzblüten-Leiste) mit Nägeln fixiert, an den Ecken jeweils Buckel in Blattform. Stehkanten dreiseitig von ornamentiertem Metallrahmen (Eierstabmuster) umfaßt, Messingschließe mit Kettengliedverzierung erhalten, grün-gelbes Kapital, dreiseitiger Goldschnitt (punziertes Rautenmuster), Pergamentvorsatz. - 82x58mm.

Bl.1a unterhalb des rot gedruckten Titels Wappen in Deckfarbenmalerei: Tropfenumrissform, darin rote heraldische Lilie auf gelb-grün gespaltenem Grund (verblichen), flankiert von Monogramm L A. Unterkircher konnte das Wappen für Venedig nicht identifizieren (S.103), wies aber auf die Wiederholung der Wappenlilien in den gedruckten Holzschnittleisten Bl.k8a und t3a hin. Seine Vermutung eines Zusammenhangs bereits mit der Entstehung des Druckes läßt sich bestätigen: Vorlage war das Verlegersignet von Lucantonio Giunta (die florentinische Lilie, vgl. Husung 151-155), der die meisten Drucke Johann Emerichs in Auftrag gab, auch die unmittelbar vor und nach dem vorliegenden Druck entstandenen Officium-Ausgaben (GW 13382 und GW 13388 im Impressum genannt, GW 13384 und GW 13387 Verlegermarke unterhalb des Titels). Das Wappen ist daher als Beweis der Verlegertätigkeit L. A. Giuntas auch für diese Ausgabe und nicht als Vorbesitzereintrag zu deuten. - Im 19. Jh in der Fideikommissbibliothek Habsburg-Lothringen: auf Bl.1a zwei Stempel dieser Bibliothek.
1921 durch Zuweisung der Fideikommissbibliothek an die Nationalbibliothek (zunächst Cod. Ser. n. 13249, 312-310) gelangt.

provenance.note: inscription in brown ink on the title page of the Brevissima introductio (α1r): «Hic Liber est meus [I]acobus de Prosperosii»; below, another sixteenth-century inscription in brown ink, possibly of a religious institution: «questo libro e san F[...]ce?»
provenance.bindingNote:
Sixteenth-century parchment; rebacked probably in the eighteenth/nineteenth century with whiter parchment; manuscript title in black ink along the spine, from the tail up: «LIBER PRAECUM AD B. MARIAM VIRG.». The book was restored in the twentieth century; probably at that stage thirteenth-century manuscript parchment bifolia were detached from the inside of the binding and bound as endleaves. Now pastedowns and three further leaves of paper have been inserted at the front and at the end. The original manuscript rear pastedown, to which ξ8 is glued, is now bound at the front. Therefore the original pastedowns have been preserved by the restaurer but have been inverted. The former owners' inscriptions on α1 of the Brevissima introductio, however, suggest that that gathering must have been bound at the front of the Horae since the sixteenth century.    
Two Italian paper labels are found on the front cover: in the lower part of the board, part of a rectangular label with printed numbering: «[missing] | [part of a Roman numeral] | 27» where the printed 7 is corrected to 8 in pen; the second label, in the upper part of the board, is octagonal, edged in a light blue frame «D | V | 15»; both belong to the same collection, probably a local aristocratic family, though we should exclude the possibility that they belong to the library of the seminary itself, in consideration of the same typology (Capital letter | Roman numeral | Arabic numeral); several other sixteenth-century books present the rectangular one, as kindly observed by the Librarian of the Seminary, Dr. Elena Gurrieri.

provenance.note: inscription in brown ink in the upper margin of α2r of the Brevissima introductio «Bibliothece Florentine Domus Probationis [...] [...]».

The library of the seminary was created in 1783 with the donation by the Grand Duke of Tuscany Peter Leopold (Vienna 1747-1792) of the book holdings of the suppressed convent of the Cistercians 'del Cestello', rich in fifteenth (74 incunables are now in the library) to seventeenth editions. This book does not present the traditional ownership note «Bibliothecae Cistelli», however the rebinding operation may be responsible for the lack of evidence. Another part of the collection comes from Abbot Ferdinando Ughelli (1594-1670), the famous author of Italia Sacra; therefore this other provenance should not be excluded.

generalNotes: Title from caption on leaf a8 verso.

Publisher's name from note printed in Middle French on leaf A1 recto, which reads in full:  A la louenge de dieu de sa tressaincte [sic] et glorieuse mere / & a ledification de tous bo[n]s catholiques furent commencees ces presen=tes heures par le commandement du roy notre sire pour Anthoine Verard libraire de=mourant sur le pont nostredame a lymage saint Jehan leuangeliste ou au palais au premiier [sic] pilier deuant ou on chante la messe de messeigneurs [sic] les presidens a paris.
Woodcut device of Anthoine Vérard on leaf n8 verso.

A variant setting in the last line of caption in the lower border of leaf A1 recto signalled by GW 13295 from Cambridge University Library copy.
20 large woodcuts (of which two repeated), 37 small woodcuts (of which two repeated), multiple-piece woodcut ornamental and historiated border to each page.
Signatures: A⁸ a-n⁸ [per]⁸.  Only first and third leaves of each gathering signed ["A.i" and "A.ii" etc.]

[Oraisons], in Middle French, incipit "Jesus soit en ma teste et mon entendement", incipit "Qui tout son cueur met en dieu", A1r;  [Caption providing imprints information],in Middle French, A1r;  [Oraisons], in Middle French, caption "Oraison a la vierge marie de lacteur de ces presentes heures", incipit "[P]Rincesse de hault parage", A1v-A4r;  "Petit almanach pour .xx. ans", i.e. 1488-1508, in Middle French, A4v;  [Zodiac man], with captions in Middle French, A5r;  Benedictio, in Latin, with Holy Grail woodcut, A5v;  [Calendarium], in Middle French, A6r-A8v;  [Sequentiae evangeliorum], in Latin, a1r-a3v;  "Passio domini nostri iesu christi secundum Johannem", in Latin, a3v-a7v;  [Oratio], in Latin, incipit "Deus qui manus tuas et pedes tuos", in Latin, a7v;  "Oraison pour le sieures tres= deuote", in Latin, incipit "[A]Nte portam hierusalem sedebat san=ctus petrus", a8r;  Horae Beatae Virginis Mariae, in Latin, a8v-f4v, including the [Officium] de sancta Cruce, c1r-v, the [Officium] de Spiritu Sancto, c2r-v, the [Officium] de conceptione Beatae Mariae Virginis, c3r-v, and [Mutationes in Officio Beatae Virginis Mariae], e4v-f4v;  Septem psalmi poenitentiales, in Latin, f5r-g2v;  Litaniae sanctorum et orationes, in Latin, g2v-g7r;  Officium mortuorum, in Latin, g7v-i7v;  [Suffragia], in Latin, i8r-k2r;  Orationes et Contemplatio Mariae Virgins, in Latin, k2v-k5v;  [Litaniae lauretanae], incipit "[M]Jssus est gabriel angelus", k5v-l1r, in Latin, preceded by caption and text in Middle French, k5v-k6r, and followed by two orations in Latin, k8v-l1r;  [Suffragia sanctorum], in Latin, l1r-l7r;  [Orationes], in Latin with captions in Middle French, l7r-m2r;  Gregorius I, Pont. Max. [?]. Orationes sancti Gregorii, in Latin, with captions in Middle French, m2r-m3r;  [Orationes], in Latin with captions in Middle French, caption "Sensuiuent cinq belles oraisons que monseign[eu]r saint iehan leuangeliste fist en lonneur de la vierge Marie ...", incipit "[M]Ediatrix omnium [et] fons viuus", incipit "[A]Uxiliatrix omnium", incipit "[R]Eparatrix debilium", incipit "[I]Lluminatrix peccatorum", incipit "[A]Lleuiatrix peccatorum", m3r-m4v;  [Orationes], in Middle French and Latin, m4v-m8v;  "Office de nostre dame de pitié", in Middle French, incipit "[V]Ous vrays catholiques et deuotz seruiteurs", m8v-n4r;  "Comment pour dire de cueur & de bouche troys veritez nous nous mettons en e=stat de grace et hors de peche mortel", in Middle French, incipit "[SJIre iay peche ainsy et ainsy co[n]tre vostre bonte", n4r-v;  [Orationes], in Middle French, caption "Sensuiuent cinq belles oraisons", incipit "[M]On dieu mon pere mon createur ie me confesse auoir este", n4v-n5v;  [Arnoul Gréban]. [Lay de nostre dame], verse in Middle French, incipit "[E]N protestant de la haulte excelle[n]ce", n5v-n8r;  [Verse], in Middle French, incipit "En la parfin de loeuure louer dieu / Chacun de nous doit pour auoir sa grace", 8 lines of verse, with publisher's woodcut device, n8v;  Septem psalmi poenitentiales, in Middle French, incipit "[D]Omine ne in furore tuo arguas me. [et]c[etera]. Sire en ta fureur ne me argue", [per]1r-[per]7r;  "Oraison tres deuote a nostre seigneur", in Middle French, incipit "[S]Jre dieu createur du ciel et de la ter=re", [per]7r-[per]8v. records.physicalDescriptionNote:
West European incunabula: 60 original leaves from the presses of the Netherlands, France, Iberia and Great Britain, described by Konrad Haebler ; translated from the German by André Barbey.
This is copy number 84, of an edition of 100. Consists of 60 incunabula leaves, window-mounted with mounted printed caption label. Accompanied by a volume of text consisting of a list of the plates, arranged under country alphabetically by place of printing, with a short history of the early printing in each country followed by descriptive notes on each specimen, giving information about the printer and the character of the types.
The plates are unbound, stored together with the introductory text, within an original linen folding box, lettered on front and spine.

shelfmark.note: Sul verso della prima carta di guardia due precedenti collocazioni, una barrata: 'H 6 h 15', e più sotto: ' R/e/21'.

provenance.note: Al centro del piatto anteriore è incollata l'etichetta della attuale Biblioteca indicante la provenienza Cicogna. Sul recto della carta di guardia anteriore ampia nota manoscritta di E.A. Cicogna: 'Il presente officio in membrana impresso a Lione del 1499 era mancante di due pagine nel principio dell'officio della Madonna, e di una pagina alla fine ov'è l'orazione di Sant'Anselmo, avea tagliate fuori nel contorno marginale alcuni legni per lo più raffiguranti il sudario; e ha poi qua e la alcune figurine cancellate col dito p.e. il diavolo davanti Gesù Cristo, S. Francesco, la Beata Vergine, S. Apollonia ec. Quando io posteriormente trovavo un esemplare cartaceo dello stesso officio vi ho rimesse le tre carte o pagine mancanti, ho rimesse ne' margini le figurine del sudario, e ho innestate quelle carte che avevano le figurine nitide per contrapporle alle cancellate. Emmanuele Cicogna a. 1847'.
provenance.msNote: Sul verso della prima carta di guardia: 'Provienza Raccolta Cicogna'.

generalNotes: Title from title page on leaf [a1] recto.
The incipit of the Horae Beatae Virginis Mariae reads as follows:  Incipiunt hore b[ea]te Marie / virginis s[e]c[un]d[u]m vsum ecclesie / Sarum.

Imprints from colophon on leaf [rum8] recto [?], which reads in full:  Jmpressum venetijs per Jo/hanne[m] hertzog Jmpe[n]sis fa/mosoru[m] viror[um] Gerardi ber/reuelt [et] fridrici de egmont / Anno d[omi]ni Mccccxciiij.
Woodcut device of Fredericus de Egmondt and Gerardus Barrevelt on leaf a1 recto.  For de Egmondt's and Barrevelt's device, see BM 15th cent., V, 423.
Woodcut device D of Johannes Hamman in red on leaf [rum8] verso [?].  For Hamman's device D, see BM 15th cent., V, 423.
All recorded copies are fragmentary, many extracted from bindings made by Oldham's 'Foliage Staff Binder': see Rogers, "Johann Hamman at Venice...", 1970, pp. 363-366, with suggested collation.

Woodcut illustrations seemengly as follows:  Virgin and Child in glory, Trinity, Annunciation, St. Helena adoring the True Cross, St. Jerome [twice] and Pietà, on leaves a1 verso, b6 verso, c4 verso, r7 verso, t5 verso and [con3] verso, and [rum 3] verso.
Woodcut initials with reserved decoration or foliate design.
E. Hoskins, Horae beatae Mariae virginis, or Sarum and York Primers : with kindred books, and Primers of the reformed Roman use, together with an introduction, London, 1901, pp. xxiii-xxv
D. Rogers, "Johann Hamman at Venice: A Survey of  His Career. With a Note on the Sarum 'Horae' of 1494", in Essays in Honour of Victor Scholderer, ed. D. E. Rhodes, Mainz, 1970, 349-68, pp. 363-366

Fragments only:  a) part of a half sheet, 207 x 58 mm., containing the upper part of two leaves [leaves r7-r8], and a small portion of a third leaf [leaf r2], i.e. the end of the Commendationes animarum, the woodcut of St. Helena adoring the True Cross and a portion of the first of the Psalmi de passione;  b) part of a half sheet, 290 x 238 mm., containing six leaves of text [leaves s2-s3 and s5-s8] and the inner woodcut border of two others [leaves s1 and s4], i.e. portions of the Psalmi de passione: see Hoskins, Horae beatae Mariae virginis ..., 1901, p. xxiii, and Rogers, "Johann Hamman at Venice...", 1970, p. 365.

Oates records a similar inscription from 'your louing ness Elysabeth', probably on c3v but now largely illegible. On i8r: 'G[ulielmus] H[enrico, i.e. Henry Howard] Parrus eques Surrȩe tibi donauerat, et nunc Sum Comitis fueram qui modo Parre tuus'. On l6r four lines of verse beginning 'Parrus eques dedit hunc grato in munere libru[m] Surreo comiti, nil facit ille nouum ... 1530 Idibus octobris.' Similar inscription on p4r. On p4v: 'brother et es anolld sayeng that owt of syt owt of mynd but I troste in yow I chall not fynd et treu mawd parr [i.e. Maud Parr, wife of Sir Thomas]'. Annotation: Old shelfmark, 'G.3.61' on a3r. Text added in contemporary MS on h2v. provenance.note: Inc.5.E.2.2[2815]: Provenance: Bought from Thomas Toon in July 1888 for £8-0-0, using money from the Rustat Fund (note on front free end paper). First page inscribed 'P: Aerlebout Petrus Aerlebout Pastor in Driel 1682'. A similar inscription on y6r is dated '11 Junij 1682'. At the end of the volume is the inscription 'dit booc hoirt den besloten Conuenten der susteren van Sinte vrselen binnen Cschyedam Hyllegont symon Ians dochter'. Decoration: Principal initials illuminated with pink, blue and green colouring and red pen-flourishes in post-Renaissance style; nineteenth-century? Other initials supplied in alternating blue and red; capital strokes supplied and headings underlined in red. Device hand coloured. UkCU,SSS.19.16: Provenance: Bookplates of Francis Freeling and Samuel Sandars; printed label (1896) of Sandars bequest. In the possession of 'a gentleman at Harlem' in 1756 when it was examined on behalf of Jacob Bryant. No. 1171 in Freeling's sale catalogue (1836). Subsequently lot 202 in the sale of W. Jones Thomas (1891); bought from Ridler by Sandars in December of that year for £7.10s. See The Library, 5th series, II, p. 194-195 and III, p. 65-66. Annotations: Notes on front free end papers in the hands of Freeling and Sandars. On second front fly leaf verso a forged provenance inscription in an eighteenth-century hand: 'Ex Liber [sic] Monasterii Harlamei'. On d6r a further forged inscription in Dutch signed 'Gherard tomasz pieters zoe[n]' purporting to record the purchase of this volume from his cousin 'coster ian zoe[n]'.  MS text in Dutch, probably genuine, on k4v. At the end is a forged colophon, apparently stamped from a block: '[G]epre[n]t toe harlem bi mi laur[en]z ia[n]zon coster. m.cccc.l.' Decoration: Principal initials supplied in blue with flourishes in red and green. Other initials supplied in alternating red and blue. The forged colophon is decorated in a similar style.

provenance.bindingNote: Contemporary Venetian blind-tooled leather over bevelled wooden boards, re-backed; two sets of quintuple fillets form a double frame, withing the inner frame a repeated knotted cross; a clasp hanging from the middle of the upper cover, a metal catch in the lower cover; strips from a fairly contemporary Latin manuscript have been used to reinforce the binding and are still visible.
provenance.note: Notes in elementary cursive Italian hand, with a mercantesca base, on the first front endleaf in light brown ink: «Iste liber e[s]t mei Ioanes An | tonii Lambardo de domini | * quondam domini Francis[ci]i | et domini Marci et»; on the second front endleaf: «Afaciate un poco che non sanza dio | che  ti spagna re(?) per che | non tralaci non veogna di nomi spagnol ci | eco che som facio ea(?) eni me ripasi | loldato Christo che sole useo(?) | mi trovo consolato zolia facio | parlami chon esso sino che per dio | tigno la finestra nela facia».

on the first verso endleaf his bibliographical note: «4326 Marii Philelphi officiu(m) marie virginis et crucis et sp(irit)us sancti cum septe(m) psalmis et passione in versu thoscano»; on 103v: «Este libro assí enquadernado costo en Venecia 10 beços a dos de hebrero de 1530 y el ducado español vale 280 beços. Esta registrado 4326». In Segura Morera et al.’s catalogue the date given, 1520 instead of 1530, appears to be a typo, as a number of other manuscripts were bought in Venice and the Veneto in 1530 by Colón. 
The first substantial purchases of Colón in Venice occurred in 1521; he had instructed the Genoese merchant and banker Ottaviano Grimaldi (†1576) to ship the books to Seville via Cadiz. Unfortunately they were lost at sea; fortunately, however, they had already been registered and are listed in Hernando Colón, Memorial de los libros naufragados o Registro antiguo o Registrum A (1521, Feb-Nov.), Seville, Bibl. Colombina, MS 10-1-3; JOSÉ FRANCISCO SÁEZ GUILLÉN, Catálogo de manuscritos de la Biblioteca Colombina de Sevilla, Seville, Cabildo de la S.M. Y P.I. Catedral de Sevilla Institución Colombina, 2002, no. 620; KLAUS WAGNER, El itinerario de Hernando Colón segund sus anotaciones. Datos para la biografia del bibliofilo sevillano, «Archivo Hispalense», LXVI, no. 203, 1984 for 1983, pp. 81-99; ID., Hernando Colón: semblanza de un bibliófilo y de su biblioteca en el quinientos aniversario de su nacimiento, in El libro antiguo español. Actas del segundo Coloquio Internacional (Madrid), ed. María Luisa López-Vidriero and Pedro M. Cátedra, Salamanca, Ediciones de la Universidad de Salamanca, Biblioteca nacional de Madrid, Sociedad española de historia del libro, 1992, II, pp. 475-492.
A second trip to Venice took place in 1530, when he bought part of the collection of Marin Sanudo.
provenance.priceNote: Purchased in Venice in 1530

provenance.note:
Colón's library was deposited in 1544 at the Dominican convent of San Pablo, then passed to the Chapter of Seville in 1552. Colón had 15,000 books by the end of his life, with a special interest in vernacular languages, popular literature and cheap printing; JUAN GUILLÉN, Hernando Colón: humanismo y bibliofilia, Sevilla, Fundación José Manuel Lara, 2004, pp. 249-267. 
Sevilla, Biblioteca Colombina; old shelfmarks: J-37-30; BB-147-36; JUAN GUILLÉN TORRALBA, Historia de las Bibliotecas Capitular y Colombina, Sevilla, Fundación José Manuel Lara, 2006, pp. 107-176.

provenance.note: Inscribed 'Johan[nes] vam loe p[rae]sb[ite]r' in red and 'Jo[hannes] vam Loe p[rae]sb[ite]r' in black ink on leaf a1 recto and verso respectively, Germany, late 15th or early sixteenth, identifiable as Johannes van Loe, a Franciscan in Marl in the district of Recklinghausen in North Rhine-Westphalia. Inscribed 'Pro Conuentu Fr[atru]m Minor[um] de obseruantia In Dursten' on leaf a1 recto, and 'Convent[us] F[ratrum] minorum Durstenae. anathema auferenti' on leaf a2 recto, Dursten, Westphalia, Germany, late 15th or early sixteenth century and seventeenth century respectively, i.e. from the Library of the Franciscan Observants at Dorsten, Westphalia [the monastery was founded in 1488 and is the world's oldest permanently existing cloister of the Franciscan order]. Twentieth-century printed book label: Presented by John Charrington, M.A., Trinity Coll., 1916. [i.e.: John Charrington (1856-1939)]. Decoration: decorative initials red rubricated, red capital strokes. Initial on sig. a3 two-colour. Annotation: Very occassional near-contemorary annotations (cf. sig. e3r). Water damaged.
provenance.bindingNote: early sixteenth-century full calf over wooden boards; boards heavily bevelled top, bottom and fore-edge; triple blind fillet to form a central panel; diapered with triple blind fillet; outer border of panel decorated with repeating blind tools: five-petal flower tool with stem forming circle border (12mm) and distinctive ivy leaf tool with stem forming circle border (11mm); central lozenges decorated with blind tools: five-petal flower within circular border (13mm); bee within circular border, within square border (14mm x 13mm); tooled metal clasp (hinged on lower board); evidence of bosses removed from upper and lower boards; two metal hoops on bottom edge of upper and lower boards - presumably once chained; original endpapers removed (rear lifted and retained) and replaced; sewn onto three double raised cords; rebacked with reversed calf, spine entirely replaced; green spine label: Pastoralia Gregorii Passa 1498.

generalNotes: Früher zweiter Teil eines Sammelbandes, erster Teil herausgerissen.
Bl.N1b Eintrag "Daß bet ist guet mit fasten unnd allmußen geben" (Kurrent, 18. Jh).

Gotischer Halblederband: braunes Leder über Holz, Hälfte der Holzdeckel blank, Blinddruck (sehr abgerieben): Jagdrolle (Jäger mit Tieren, Gitter). Reste von 2 Schließen. - Mazal: Süddeutschland, Umkreis Memmingen, ähnlich Kyriss 110, Werkstatt "Wappen rund" - im Vergleich mit EBDB w000143 (r000488) jedoch nicht eindeutig. - 195x130mm.

Innendeckel und Bl.V1a zwei datierte Besitzeinträge: "Dass Buch gehörtt in das wirdig Gotzhause und dene Andechtige Schwesteren in dem Thalbach bey Bregentz gelegen - 1477(sic)" und 1727. Im 1436 gegründeten Franziskanerinnen-Kloster Thalbach bei Bregenz war seit Ende des 16. Jhs die Marienstatue „Sedes Sapientiae“ Wallfahrtsziel.
Wohl nach Aufhebung des Frauenklosters 1782 an die Hofbibliothek gelangt.

Mazal, Otto: Österreichische Nationalbibliothek, Inkunabelkatalog (ÖNB-Ink). Wiesbaden 2004, Bd. 1, S.41. - Einbanddatenbank EBDB. Verbundprojekt zur Erschließung von Einbanddurchreibungen von Bucheinbänden des 15. und 16. Jahrhunderts. http://www.hist-einband.de/?ws=w000143.

records.physicalDescriptionNote: Folios 7, 35 and 152 are missing. At the end of the text on folio 153 recto, a fragment from folio 152 (?) has been pasted in.
